data.name: CP.SrcCahierLatency
data.value: Reflex, VRR and the render queue lower system latency without costing frames per second. How much depends on the game: DrDXT measures it on your machine instead of announcing it.

data.name: CP.SrcCahierPowerPlan
data.value: The High performance plan avoids the micro-stutter caused by core parking in the Balanced plan. A gain only on a badly set machine, close to zero otherwise.

data.name: CP.SrcX3d
data.value: On an X3D processor with two core blocks (7950X3D, 9950X3D), a game placed on the block without extra cache loses frames: about 6 % on average at 1080p on a 7950X3D without core parking (Hardware Busters, April 2023, https://hwbusters.com/cpu/amd-ryzen-9-7950x3d-core-parking-problem-solution/6/). The gap depends on the game: DrDXT measures it on your machine instead of announcing it.

data.name: CP.SrcNvPowerLimit
data.value: Lowering the power limit makes the card run cooler and draw less. No public measurement found puts a number on the frame loss at 90 %: DrDXT measures it on your machine and undoes the setting if it costs anything.

data.name: CP.SrcNs1Os
data.value: A Windows setting, reversible, on every card. The effect varies with the game and the machine, no number is promised. DrDXT's A/B measures frames per second: a latency-only gain does not show up in it.

data.name: CP.SrcEcranFrequence
data.value: Microsoft (learn.microsoft.com, ChangeDisplaySettingsEx): CDS_TEST asks Windows whether the mode can be set without setting it; CDS_UPDATEREGISTRY stores the mode in the user's profile. The mode set is one Windows lists for the display at its current resolution (EnumDisplaySettings). No frame gain is announced.

data.name: CP.SrcPagefile
data.value: Microsoft (learn.microsoft.com, introduction to page files): the commit limit is RAM plus page files; when it is reached, freezes, crashes and other failures. The page file is also used for blue-screen dumps. This is reliability: no frame gain is announced.

data.name: CP.SrcPreferMaxPerf
data.value: The NVIDIA driver's "Power management mode" setting (PREFERRED_PSTATE, official header NvApiDriverSettings.h). No primary source puts a number on an in-game gain: it is unknown, and DrDXT measures it in game before keeping it.

data.name: CP.SrcHeuresActives
data.value: Microsoft (learn.microsoft.com, "Manage device restarts after updates"): automatic restarts after an update happen outside active hours; 18 hours at most. No frame gain: this is comfort.

data.name: CP.SrcCpuPowerCap
data.value: Intel SDM vol. 4 (MSR_PKG_POWER_LIMIT 0x610, PL1 = sustained limit); DrDXT measurement, game slowed by heat second by second (IA32_PACKAGE_THERM_STATUS 0x1B1).

data.name: CP.SrcModeBoost
data.value: Microsoft (learn.microsoft.com, "PERFBOOSTMODE"): the value 0 disables the processor boost, whatever its control mode. Its in-game effect on a recent processor is not published: DrDXT measures it on your PC.

data.name: CP.Gain01
data.value: High performance power plan: removes the micro-stutter from core parking in the Balanced plan. Close to zero on a well-set modern PC; a real fix only when the machine is badly set. Safe everywhere.

data.name: CP.Gain02
data.value: Wireless card taken out of its power-saving mode (plugged-in value of the active plan) when the game goes through Wi-Fi. Microsoft: power saving "reduces power consumption at the cost of increased transfer latency". Latency comfort, not extra frames; set and read back; the battery value is never touched. Reversible.

data.name: CP.Gain03
data.value: Processor sustained power limit (PL1) raised to the peak the board allows (PL2). TechPowerUp (i9-14900K, RTX 4090, PL1 = PL2 forced): 65 W costs 15.5 % of frames at 720p and about 16 % at 1080p, 125 W about 2 %. Offered on an Intel desktop only, when PL1 reads below PL2 with no lock; measured in game, put back without a gain.

data.name: CP.Gain04
data.value: Processor sustained limit (PL1) capped at the last game's median plus a third, when that game was slowed by heat and the board allows far more. The expected gain is less time throttled, not more frames: no published number; set on click, read back by the doctor over the next games.

data.name: CP.Gain05
data.value: Processor boost turned off in the power plan, put back to that plan's default. Offered only on a desktop, when it reads off while the plan's default allows it; never on a laptop, where turning it off often serves heat and noise. Gain unknown, measured in game and undone if it gains nothing. Reversible.

data.name: CP.Gain06
data.value: Disabled page file put back under automatic management by Windows: without it, committed memory caps at RAM and a demanding game can freeze or crash. Reliability, not extra frames. Offered only when it reads disabled. Takes effect after a restart. Reversible.

data.name: CP.Gain07
data.value: Windows Update active hours set to the hours of the recorded games: Windows does not restart the PC automatically during those hours. Comfort, not extra frames. Offered only when recorded games fall outside the current hours. Windows Update stays on. Reversible.

data.name: CP.Gain08
data.value: Game display put back to the highest refresh rate Windows offers at its current resolution. Offered only when it reads lower. Windows tries it first, DrDXT reads it back, and without confirmation within 15 seconds the previous mode returns. Smoothness, no frame number. Reversible.

data.name: CP.Gain09
data.value: VRR + Vsync + frame cap below the display's refresh rate: low, steady system latency without losing frames per second. All cards, no overclock.

data.name: CP.Gain10
data.value: Render queue floor: less delay between your mouse and the screen. All cards, no overclock.

data.name: CP.Gain11
data.value: Hardware-accelerated GPU scheduling turned on: can lower render latency on cards that support it; the effect depends on the card, the driver and the game. Takes effect after a restart. Reversible.

data.name: CP.Gain12
data.value: Windows pointer acceleration turned off: the cursor follows the motion exactly, whatever the speed; aim keeps the same scale. No latency or frame gain: accuracy. Takes effect at the next sign-in. Reversible.

data.name: CP.Gain13
data.value: Windows Game Mode turned on: Windows gives priority to the running game; light effect, varies with the machine. Takes effect at the next game launch. Reversible.

data.name: CP.Gain14
data.value: Game DVR background recording turned off: removes the permanent capture and frees processor and graphics card time. Manual capture stays possible. Reversible.

data.name: CP.Gain15
data.value: Variable refresh rate + optimizations for windowed games (flip model) turned on: less latency in windowed or borderless mode. The VRR part only applies if G-Sync or FreeSync is on in the driver; the flip model applies without it. Auto HDR kept. Reversible.

data.name: CP.Gain16
data.value: Fixes bad CCD parking by the AMD 3D V-Cache service, CPPC and the Game Bar, with no BIOS write. Only when it is badly set; the only public measurement found gives about 6 % at 1080p (see the source). The real gain is proven by the A/B re-measurement on your machine, never assumed.

data.name: CP.Gain17
data.value: Maximum performance in the game's profile only (never globally): the card does not clock down during the game. Useful only if it clocks down; gain unknown, measured in game and undone if it gains nothing. Offered only when the setting is read and not already on "Prefer maximum performance". Reversible.

data.name: CP.Gain18
data.value: Power limit lowered: the card runs cooler and draws less. Its effect on frames has no public measurement: it is measured in game on your machine, and the setting is undone if it costs anything. Efficiency and heat, not a frame gain.

data.name: CP.Gain19
data.value: Power saver plan left for Balanced, Windows' default plan, on a desktop PC only. No frame gain is published: your matches show what it brings. Reversible.

data.name: CP.Gain20
data.value: Page file handed back to the system drive when it sits on a hard drive and Windows on an SSD (the "Automatically manage" value). Reliability and smoothness outside games; takes effect at restart. Reversible.
